subproblem.title: Tonelli–Fatou: lower left difference quotients have a.e. finite liminf over j
subproblem.statement: Let μ_j (j ∈ ℕ) be Borel measures on ℝ, let a, b ∈ ℝ and let Λ ∈ [0, ∞) satisfy μ_j([a, b]) ≤ Λ for every j. For t ∈ ℝ and j ∈ ℕ let S_j(t) := liminf_{h→0+} ENNReal.ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ_j((t − h, t)) ∈ [0, ∞] (limit inferior in [0, ∞] along h → 0 with h > 0, i.e. along 𝓝[>] 0). Then for Lebesgue-almost every t ∈ ℝ: if a < t < b, then liminf_{j→∞} S_j(t) ≠ ∞.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (μ : ℕ → Measure ℝ) (a b : ℝ) (Λ : ℝ≥0∞), Λ ≠ ∞ → (∀ j, μ j (Icc a b) ≤ Λ) → ∀ᵐ t ∂(volume : Measure ℝ), t ∈ Ioo a b → liminf (fun j => liminf (fun h : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹ * μ j (Ioo (t - h) t)) (𝓝[>] 0)) atTop ≠ ∞
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 0 and 4, and the comparison in step 7, of the parent-supplied proof of cmc_fc_good_slice. These are the measurable majorants of the slice quantity (lim infs of difference quotients) controlled by Tonelli and Fatou, which realize elementarily the Fatou/Tonelli ingredient of Simon Ch. 6, proof of 7.2. The hypothesis a < b is not needed: if b ≤ a, the implication is vacuous. Notation: S_j(t) := liminf_{h→0+} ENNReal.ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ_j((t − h, t)) ∈ [0, ∞], the limit inferior along the filter 𝓝[>] 0. "Almost every" refers to Lebesgue measure Leb on ℝ, and ∫⁻ denotes the [0, ∞]-valued Lebesgue integral.

1. (Restriction.) For j ∈ ℕ let ν_j := μ_j⌞[a, b], i.e. ν_j(E) = μ_j(E ∩ [a, b]) for Borel E. Then ν_j(ℝ) = μ_j([a, b]) ≤ Λ < ∞. So ν_j is a finite (in particular σ-finite and s-finite) Borel measure, and ν_j(E) = μ_j(E) for every Borel E ⊆ [a, b].

2. (Measurability and Tonelli.) Fix j and h ≥ 0, and let E_h := {(t, x) ∈ ℝ × ℝ : t − h < x and x < t}. It is open, being defined by strict inequalities between continuous functions, hence Borel. For fixed t, its section {x : (t, x) ∈ E_h} is the interval (t − h, t). For fixed x, its section {t : (t, x) ∈ E_h} is (x, x + h), since t − h < x < t ⟺ x < t < x + h. Because ν_j is s-finite, t ↦ ν_j((t − h, t)) = ν_j({x : (t, x) ∈ E_h}) is Borel measurable (Mathlib measurable_measure_prodMk_left). Now compute the product measure Leb ⊗ ν_j of E_h by integrating the sections in either order (Mathlib Measure.prod_apply and Measure.prod_apply_symm; both factors are σ-finite):
  ∫⁻ ν_j((t − h, t)) dt = (Leb ⊗ ν_j)(E_h) = ∫⁻ Leb((x, x + h)) dν_j(x) = ∫⁻ ENNReal.ofReal(h) dν_j(x) = ENNReal.ofReal(h)·ν_j(ℝ).

3. (First application of Fatou.) For n ∈ ℕ put h_n := 1/(n + 1) > 0. For t ∈ ℝ put Q_{j,n}(t) := (n + 1)·ν_j((t − h_n, t)) ∈ [0, ∞], with n + 1 read in [0, ∞]. By step 2, Q_{j,n} is measurable. In [0, ∞] we have (n + 1)·ENNReal.ofReal(1/(n + 1)) = 1, and a constant factor may be pulled out of the integral of a measurable function (Mathlib lintegral_const_mul). Hence step 2 gives
  ∫⁻ Q_{j,n} = (n + 1)·ENNReal.ofReal(h_n)·ν_j(ℝ) = ν_j(ℝ) ≤ Λ.
Let q_j(t) := liminf_{n→∞} Q_{j,n}(t). It is measurable as a sequential liminf of measurable functions (Mathlib Measurable.liminf). Fatou's lemma (Mathlib lintegral_liminf_le) gives ∫⁻ q_j ≤ liminf_n ∫⁻ Q_{j,n} = ν_j(ℝ) ≤ Λ.

4. (Second application of Fatou.) The function t ↦ liminf_{j→∞} q_j(t) is measurable, again by Measurable.liminf. By Fatou's lemma again, ∫⁻ liminf_j q_j ≤ liminf_j ∫⁻ q_j ≤ Λ < ∞; the last liminf is ≤ Λ because each of its terms is ≤ Λ by step 3. A measurable [0, ∞]-valued function with finite integral is finite almost everywhere (Mathlib ae_lt_top). Hence there is a Lebesgue-null set Z such that liminf_j q_j(t) < ∞ for every t ∉ Z.

5. (Comparison S_j ≤ q_j on (a, b).) Fix t with a < t < b and fix j ∈ ℕ. The sequence h_n = 1/(n + 1) tends to 0 (Mathlib tendsto_one_div_add_atTop_nhds_zero_nat) through positive values, i.e. h_n → 0 along 𝓝[>] 0. For any u : ℝ → [0, ∞], the liminf of u along 𝓝[>] 0 is at most the liminf of the sequence u(h_n) (Mathlib Filter.Tendsto.liminf_le_liminf_comp). With u(h) := ENNReal.ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ_j((t − h, t)) this gives
  S_j(t) ≤ liminf_n ENNReal.ofReal(h_n⁻¹)·μ_j((t − h_n, t)).
Since t − a > 0 and h_n → 0, we have h_n ≤ t − a for all sufficiently large n. For such n, (t − h_n, t) ⊆ [a, b] because t − h_n ≥ a and t < b, so μ_j((t − h_n, t)) = ν_j((t − h_n, t)) by step 1. Also ENNReal.ofReal(h_n⁻¹) = ENNReal.ofReal(n + 1) = n + 1. So the sequence on the right agrees with Q_{j,n}(t) for all sufficiently large n. A liminf along atTop depends only on eventual values (Mathlib Filter.liminf_congr), so its liminf equals q_j(t). Hence S_j(t) ≤ q_j(t).

6. (Conclusion.) Let t ∉ Z and suppose a < t < b. By step 5, S_j(t) ≤ q_j(t) for every j. Since liminf is monotone, liminf_j S_j(t) ≤ liminf_j q_j(t), which is < ∞ by step 4; that is, liminf_j S_j(t) ≠ ∞. Since Z is Lebesgue-null, this holds for Lebesgue-almost every t, which is the statement. ∎
proof_key_steps: Restrict to [a, b]: ν_j := μ_j⌞[a, b] is a finite Borel measure with ν_j(ℝ) ≤ Λ that agrees with μ_j on Borel subsets of [a, b].
Tonelli on the open set E_h = {(t, x) : t − h < x < t}, whose sections are (t − h, t) and (x, x + h): t ↦ ν_j((t − h, t)) is measurable and ∫⁻ ν_j((t − h, t)) dt = ofReal(h)·ν_j(ℝ).
Q_{j,n}(t) := (n + 1)·ν_j((t − 1/(n + 1), t)) has integral ν_j(ℝ) ≤ Λ. By Fatou, q_j := liminf_n Q_{j,n} is measurable with ∫⁻ q_j ≤ Λ.
By Fatou again, ∫⁻ liminf_j q_j ≤ Λ < ∞, so liminf_j q_j(t) < ∞ for a.e. t (ae_lt_top).
For t ∈ (a, b), h_n = 1/(n + 1) → 0 in 𝓝[>] 0 and eventually (t − h_n, t) ⊆ [a, b], so S_j(t) ≤ q_j(t) (Tendsto.liminf_le_liminf_comp, liminf_congr). Hence liminf_j S_j(t) ≤ liminf_j q_j(t) < ∞ a.e.

audit.reason: The one-line Lean proposition exactly matches the stated global almost-everywhere implication and both liminf filters. Restriction supplies the finiteness needed for measurable sections and Tonelli. Quotient normalization, sequential measurability and two applications of Fatou establish a common null exceptional set. The comparison S_j ≤ q_j has the correct direction, and eventual interval containment justifies replacing the original measures by their restrictions. Monotonicity then proves the exact nested-liminf conclusion without assuming measurability of S_j. The proof is complete, independent of the other child and parent, and sufficiently explicit for formalization. The bare name is fresh.
